paragraphs.sourceText: Just because they can’t sing opera or ride a bicycle doesn’t mean that animals don’t have culture. There’s no better example of this than killer whales. As one of the most __26__ predators（食肉动物），killer whales may not fit the __27__ of a cultured creature. However, these beasts of the sea do display a vast range of highly __28__ behaviors that appear to be driving their genetic development.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不会唱戏、不会骑自行车，并不意味着动物就没有文化。没有比虎鲸更好的例子了。作为最残忍的食肉动物之一，虎鲸可能不符合养殖生物的形象。然而，这些海洋猛兽确实表现出了一系列高度精细的行为，这些行为似乎正在推动它们的基因发育。

paragraphs.sourceText: The word “culture” comes from the Latin “colere,” which __29__ means “to cultivate.” In other words, it refers to anything that is __30__ or learnt, rather than instinctive or natural. Among human populations, culture not only affects the way we live, but also writes itself into our genes, affecting who we are. For instance, having spent many generations hunting the fat marine mammals of the Arctic, the Eskimos of Greenland have developed certain genetic __31__ that help them digest and utilize this fat-rich diet, thereby allowing them to __32__ in their cold climate.
paragraphs.translationZh: “文化”一词源自拉丁语“colere”，字面意思是“培养”。换句话说，它指的是任何获得或学习的东西，而不是本能或自然的东西。在人类群体中，文化不仅影响我们的生活方式，而且将其自身写入我们的基因，影响我们是谁。例如，格陵兰岛的爱斯基摩人花了几代人的时间捕猎北极的肥胖海洋哺乳动物，他们已经发展出了某些基因适应能力，帮助他们消化和利用这种富含脂肪的饮食，从而使他们能够在寒冷的气候中茁壮成长。

paragraphs.sourceText: Like humans, killer whales have colonized a range of different __33__ across the globe, occupying every ocean basin on the planet, with an empire that __34__ from pole to pole. As such, different populations of killer whales have had to learn different hunting techniques in order to gain the upper hand over their local prey（猎物）. This, in turn, has a major effect on their diet, leading scientists to __35__ that the ability to learn population-specific hunting methods could be driving the animals’ genetic development.
paragraphs.translationZh: 和人类一样，虎鲸已经在全球范围内的不同栖息地定居，占领了地球上的每一个海洋盆地，建立了一个从两极延伸到另一极的帝国。因此，不同种群的虎鲸必须学习不同的狩猎技术，才能在当地猎物面前占据上风。反过来，这对它们的饮食产生了重大影响，科学家们推测学习特定人群狩猎方法的能力可能会推动动物的基因发育。

paragraphs.sourceText: Living with parents edges out other living arrangements for 18-to 34-year-olds
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于 18 至 34 岁的人来说，与父母同住比其他生活安排更重要

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Broad demographic (人口的)shifts is marital status, educational attainment and employment have transformed the way young adults in the U.S. are living, and a new Pew Research Center analysis highlights the implications of these changes for the most basic element of their lives—where they call home. In 2014,for the first time in more than 130 years, adults ages 18 to 34 were slightly more likely to be living in their parents’ home than they were to be living with a spouse or partner in their own household.
paragraphs.translationZh: A）广泛的人口变化是婚姻状况、教育程度和就业改变了美国年轻人的生活方式，皮尤研究中心的一项新分析强调了这些变化对他们生活中最基本要素——他们称之为家的地方的影响。 2014 年，130 多年来首次发现，18 至 34 岁的成年人住在父母家里的可能性略高于与配偶或伴侣住在自己家里的可能性。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) This turn of events is fueled primarily by the dramatic drop in the share of young Americans who are choosing to settle down romantically before age 35. Dating back to 1880, the most common living arrangement among young adults has been living with a romantic partner, whether a spouse or a significant other. This type of arrangement peaked around 1960, when 62% of the nation’s 18-to 34-year-olds were living with a spouse or partner in their own household, and only one-in-five were living with their parents.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 这一事件的发生主要是由于选择在 35 岁之前浪漫定居的美国年轻人比例急剧下降。可以追溯到 1880 年，年轻人中最常见的生活安排是与浪漫伴侣（无论是配偶还是重要的其他人）同居。这种安排在 1960 年左右达到顶峰，当时全国 18 至 34 岁的人中有 62% 与配偶或伴侣住在自己的家里，只有五分之一的人与父母住在一起。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) By 2014, 31.6% of young adults were living with a spouse or partner in their own household, below the share living in the home of their parent(s) (32.1%). Some 14% of young adults lived alone, were a single parent or lived with one or more roommates. The remaining 22% lived in the home of another family member (such as a grandparent, in-law or sibling (兄弟姐妹), a non-relative, or in group quarters like college dormitories.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 到 2014 年，31.6% 的年轻人与配偶或伴侣住在自己的家里，低于住在父母家里的比例 (32.1%)。大约 14% 的年轻人独居、单亲或与一名或多名室友住在一起。剩下的 22% 住在另一个家庭成员（例如祖父母、姻亲或兄弟姐妹）、非亲属的家里，或者住在大学宿舍等集体宿舍里。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) It’s worth noting that the overall share of young adults living with their parents was not at a record high in 2014. This arrangement peaked around 1940, when about 35% of the nation’s 18-to 34-year-olds lived with mom and/or dad (compared with 32% in 2014). What has changed, instead, is the relative share adopting different ways of living in early adulthood, with the decline of romantic coupling pushing living at home to the top of a much less uniform list of living arrangements.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 值得注意的是，2014 年年轻人与父母同住的总体比例并未创历史新高。这种安排在 1940 年左右达到顶峰，当时全国 18 至 34 岁的年轻人中约有 35% 与父母住在一起（2014 年为 32%）。相反，发生变化的是在成年早期采取不同生活方式的相对比例，随着浪漫情侣的减少，将在家生活推向了不太统一的生活安排列表的首位。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Among young adults, living arrangements differ significantly by gender. For men ages 18 to 34, living at home with mom and/or dad has been the dominant living arrangement since 2009, In 2014,28% of young men were living with a spouse of partner in their own home, while 35% were living in the home of their parent(s). Young women, however,are still more likely to be living with a spouse of romantic partner(35%) than they are to be living with their parent(s)(29%).
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 在年轻人中，生活安排因性别而有显着差异。对于18至34岁的男性来说，自2009年以来，与父母一起住在家里一直是主要的居住安排。2014年，28%的年轻男性与伴侣的配偶住在自己的家里，而35%的人住在父母的家里。然而，年轻女性更有可能与浪漫伴侣的配偶（35%）住在一起，而不是与父母（29%）住在一起。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) In 2014, more young women (16%) than young men (13%) were heading up a household without a spouse or partner.This is mainly because women are more likely than men to be single parents living with their children. For their part, young men (25%) are more likely than young women (19%) to be living in the home of another family member, a non-relative or in some type of group quarters.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 2014 年，没有配偶或伴侣的家庭的年轻女性 (16%) 多于年轻男性 (13%)。这主要是因为女性比男性更有可能成为与孩子生活在一起的单亲父母。就年轻男性（25%）而言，他们比年轻女性（19%）更有可能住在另一位家庭成员、非亲属的家中或某种类型的集体宿舍中。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) A variety of factors contribute to the long-run increase in the share of young. Adults living with the parents. The first in the postponement of, if not retreat from, marriage. The average age of first marriage has risen steadily for decades. In addition, a growing share of young adult may be avoiding marriage altogether. A previous Pew Research Center analysis projected that as many as one-in-four of today’s young adult may never marry. While cohabitation（同居）has been on the rise, the overall share of young adults either married or living with an unmarried partner has substantially fallen since 1990.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 多种因素导致年轻人比例的长期增加。与父母同住的成年人。第一个是推迟（如果不是退出的话）婚姻。几十年来，平均初婚年龄稳步上升。此外，越来越多的年轻人可能会完全避免结婚。皮尤研究中心之前的一项分析预测，当今多达四分之一的年轻人可能永远不会结婚。虽然同居现象一直在增加，但自 1990 年以来，已婚或与未婚伴侣同居的年轻人的总体比例大幅下降。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) In addition, trends in both employment status and wages have likely contributed to the growing share of young adults who are living in the home of their parent(s), and this is especially true of young men. Employed young men are much less likely to live at home than young men without a job, and employment among young men has fallen significantly in recent decades. The share of young men with jobs peaked around 1960 at 84%. In 2014, only 71% of 18-to-34-year-old men were employed. Similarly with earnings, young men’s wages (after adjusting for inflation) have been on a downward trajectory (轨迹) since 1970 and fell significantly form 2000 to 2010. As wages have fallen ,the share of young men living in the home of their parent(s) has risen.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 此外，就业状况和工资的趋势可能导致越来越多的年轻人住在父母家里，这对于年轻人来说尤其如此。与没有工作的年轻人相比，有工作的年轻人住在家里的可能性要小得多，而且近几十年来，年轻人的就业率大幅下降。青年男性有工作的比例在 1960 年左右达到顶峰，达到 84%。 2014年，18至34岁男性中只有71%有工作。与收入类似，自 1970 年以来，年轻人的工资（根据通货膨胀调整后）一直呈下降趋势，并且从 2000 年到 2010 年大幅下降。随着工资下降，住在父母家里的年轻人比例有所上升。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Economic factors seem to explain less of why young adult women are increasingly likely to live at home. Generally, young women have had growing success in the paid labor market since 1960 and hence might increasingly be expected to be a be to afford to afford to live independently of their parents. For women, delayed marriage—which is related, in part, to labor market outcomes for men—may explain more of the increase in their living in the family home.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 经济因素似乎不能解释为什么年轻成年女性越来越倾向于住在家里。一般来说，自 1960 年以来，年轻女性在有酬劳动力市场上取得了越来越大的成功，因此可能越来越被期望能够有能力独立于父母生活。对于女性来说，晚婚——这在一定程度上与男性劳动力市场的结果有关——可能更多地解释了她们在家庭住宅中生活的增加。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) The Great Recession (and modest recovery) has also been associated with an increase in young adults living at home. Initially in the wake of the recession, college enrollments expanded, boosting the ranks of young adults living at home. And given the weak job opportunities facing young adults, living at home was part of the private safety net help young adults to weather the economic storm.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 大衰退（和适度复苏）也与住在家里的年轻人的增加有关。经济衰退后，大学入学人数开始扩大，居家生活的年轻人数量不断增加。鉴于年轻人面临的就业机会较少，住在家里是帮助年轻人度过经济风暴的私人安全网的一部分。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Beyond gender, young adult’s living arrangements differ considerable by education—which is tied to financial means. For young adults without a bachelor’s degree, as of 2008 living at home with their parents was more prevalent than living with a romantic partner. By 2014, 36% of 18-to 34-year-olds who had not completed a bachelor’s degree were living with their parent(s) while 27% were living with a spouse or partner. Among college graduates, in 2014 46% were married or living with a partner, and only 19% were living with their parent(s). Young adults with a college degree have fared much better in the labor market than their less-educated counterparts, which has in turn made it easier to establish their own households.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 除了性别之外，年轻人的生活安排因教育而存在很大差异——教育与经济手段密切相关。对于没有学士学位的年轻人来说，截至 2008 年，与父母同住比与恋人同住更为普遍。到 2014 年，18 至 34 岁未完成学士学位的人中有 36% 与父母住在一起，而 27% 与配偶或伴侣住在一起。 2014年，在大学毕业生中，46%已婚或与伴侣同居，只有19%与父母同住。拥有大学学位的年轻人在劳动力市场上的表现比受教育程度较低的年轻人要好得多，这反过来又使他们更容易建立自己的家庭。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36.Unemployed young men are more likely to live with their parents than the employed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 失业青年比就业青年更有可能与父母住在一起。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37.In 2014, the percentage of men aged 18 to 34 living with their parents was greater than that of their female counterparts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 2014年，18至34岁的男性与父母同住的比例高于女性。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38.The percentage of young people who are married or live with a partner has greatly decreased in the past three decades or so.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38.在过去三十年左右的时间里，已婚或与伴侣同居的年轻人的比例大大下降。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39.Around the mid-20th century, only 20 percent of 18- to 34-year-old lived in their parents’ home.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 20 世纪中叶左右，18 至 34 岁的人中只有 20% 住在父母家里。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40.Young adults with a college degree found it easier to live independently of their parents.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40.拥有大学学位的年轻人发现更容易独立于父母生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41.Young men are less likely to end up as single parents than young women.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 年轻男性比年轻女性更不可能成为单亲父母。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42.More young adult women live with their parents than before due to delayed marriage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 由于晚婚，更多的年轻成年女性与父母住在一起。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43.The percentage of young men who live with their parents has grown due to their decreased pay in recent decades.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 近几十年来，由于工资下降，与父母住在一起的年轻男性比例有所增加。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44.The rise in the number of college students made more young adults live with their parents.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 大学生数量的增加使得更多的年轻人与父母住在一起。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45.One reason for young adults to live with their parents is that get married late or stay single all their lives.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45.年轻人与父母住在一起的原因之一是晚婚或终生单身。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: According to the majority of Americans, women are every bit as capable of being good political leaders as men. The same can be said of their ability to dominate the corporate boardroom. And according to a new Pew Research Center survey on women and leadership, most Americans find women indistinguishable from men on key leadership traits such as intelligence and capacity for innovation, with many saying they’re stronger than men in terms of being passionate and organized leaders.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大多数美国人认为，女性与男性一样有能力成为优秀的政治领导人。他们主导公司董事会的能力也是如此。皮尤研究中心关于女性和领导力的一项新调查显示，大多数美国人发现，在智力和创新能力等关键领导特质上，女性与男性没有什么区别，许多人表示，在成为充满激情和有组织性的领导者方面，她们比男性更强。

paragraphs.sourceText: So why, then, are women in short supply at the top of government and business in the United States? According to the public, at least, it’s not that they lack toughness, management talent or proper skill sets.
paragraphs.translationZh: 那么，为什么美国政府和企业高层的女性短缺呢？至少在公众看来，他们并不缺乏韧性、管理才能或适当的技能。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s also not all about work-life balance. Although economic research and previous survey findings have shown that career interruptions related to motherhood may make it harder for women to advance in their careers and compete for top executive jobs, relatively few adults in the recent survey point to this as a key barrier for women seeking leadership roles. Only about one-in-five say women’s family responsibilities are a major reason why there aren’t more females in top leadership positions in business and politics.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这也不全是工作与生活的平衡。尽管经济研究和之前的调查结果表明，与母亲身份有关的职业中断可能会使女性更难在职业生涯中取得进步并竞争高管职位，但在最近的调查中，相对较少的成年人认为这是女性寻求领导职位的主要障碍。只有约五分之一的人表示，女性的家庭责任是导致商界和政界没有更多女性担任高层领导职位的主要原因。

paragraphs.sourceText: Instead, topping the list of reasons, about four-in-ten Americans point to a double standard for women seeking to climb to the highest levels of either politics or business, where they have to do more than their male counterparts to prove themselves. Similar shares say the electorate(选民)and corporate America are just not ready to put more women in top leadership positions.
paragraphs.translationZh: 相反，最重要的原因是，大约十分之四的美国人指出，寻求攀登政界或商界最高层的女性存在双重标准，她们必须比男性同行做更多的事情来证明自己。类似的观点表示，选民和美国企业界还没有准备好让更多女性担任高层领导职务。

paragraphs.sourceText: As a result, the public is divided about whether the imbalance in corporate America will change in the foreseeable future, even though women have made major advances in the workplace. While 53% believe men will continue to hold more top executive positions in business in the future, 44% say it’s only a matter of time before as many women are in top executive positions as men. Americans are less doubtful when it comes to politics: 73% expect to see a female president in their lifetime.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，尽管女性在工作场所取得了重大进步，但公众对于美国企业界的不平衡是否会在可预见的未来改变存在分歧。虽然 53% 的人认为未来男性将继续在企业中担任更多的高管职位，但 44% 的人表示，担任高管职位的女性数量与男性一样多只是时间问题。美国人在政治方面的疑虑较少：73% 的人希望在有生之年见到一位女总统。

paragraphs.sourceText: People have grown taller over the last century, with South Korean women shooting up by more than 20cm on average, and Iranian men gaining. 16.5cm. A global study looked at the average height of 18-year-olds in 200 countries 1914 and 2014.
paragraphs.translationZh: 上个世纪以来，人们的身高不断增长，韩国女性平均增高超过 20 厘米，伊朗男性也在增加。 16.5厘米。一项全球研究调查了 1914 年和 2014 年 200 个国家 18 岁青少年的平均身高。

paragraphs.sourceText: The results reveal that while Swedes were the tallest people in the world in 1914, Dutch men have risen from 12th place to claim top spot with an average height of 182.5cm. Larvian women. Meanwhile, rose from 28th place in 1914 to become the tallest in the world a century later, with an average height of 169.8cm.
paragraphs.translationZh: 结果显示，瑞典人是 1914 年世界上最高的人，而荷兰男性则以 182.5 厘米的平均身高从第 12 位跃升至榜首。幼虫妇女。与此同时，他从1914年的第28位上升到一个世纪后成为世界上最高的人，平均身高为169.8厘米。

paragraphs.sourceText: James Bentham, a co-author of the research from Imperial College, London, says the global trend is likely to be due primarily to improvements in nutrition and healthcare. “An individual’s genetics has a big influence on their height, but once you average over whole populations, genetics plays a less key role,” he added.
paragraphs.translationZh: 伦敦帝国理工学院这项研究的合著者詹姆斯·本瑟姆表示，全球趋势可能主要归因于营养和医疗保健的改善。 “一个人的基因对其身高有很大影响，但一旦对整个人群进行平均，基因的作用就不那么重要了，”他补充道。

paragraphs.sourceText: A little extra height brings a number of advantages, says Elio Riboli of Imperial College. “Being taller is associated with longer life expectancy,” he said. “This is largely due to a lower risk of dying of cardiovascular（心血管的）disease among taller people.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 帝国理工学院的埃利奥·里博利 (Elio Riboli) 表示，稍微增加一点高度会带来许多优势。 “身高越高，预期寿命越长，”他说。 “这主要是因为较高的人死于心血管疾病的风险较低。”

paragraphs.sourceText: But while height has increased around the world, the trend in many countries of north and sub-Saharan Africa causes concern, says Riboli. While height increased in Uganda and Niger during the early 20th century, the trend has reversed in recent years, with height decreasing among 18-year-olds.
paragraphs.translationZh: 里博利表示，虽然世界各地的身高都在增加，但北非和撒哈拉以南非洲许多国家的这一趋势引起了担忧。虽然乌干达和尼日尔的身高在 20 世纪初有所增加，但近年来这一趋势发生了逆转，18 岁青少年的身高有所下降。

paragraphs.sourceText: “One reason for these decreases in height is the economic situation in the 1980s,” said Alexander Moradi of the Universith of Sussex. The nutritional and health crises that followed the policy of structural adjustment, he says, led to many children and teenagers failing to reach their full potential in terms of height.
paragraphs.translationZh: “身高下降的一个原因是 20 世纪 80 年代的经济形势，”苏塞克斯大学的亚历山大·莫拉迪 (Alexander Moradi) 说。他说，结构调整政策带来的营养和健康危机导致许多儿童和青少年未能充分发挥身高潜力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Bentham believe the global rtend of increasing height has important implications. “How tall we are now is strongly influenced by the environment we grew up in,” he said. “If we give children the best possible start in life now, they will be healthier and more productive for decades to come.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 边沁认为全球身高增长趋势具有重要意义。 “我们现在的身高很大程度上受到我们成长环境的影响，”他说。 “如果我们现在为孩子们提供最好的人生开端，他们在未来几十年将会更加健康、更加富有成效。”

options.translationZh: 大多数女性投票选举女总统。

options.sourceText: As many women in top government positions as men.
options.reflowSourceText: As many women in top government positions as men.
options.translationZh: 担任政府高层职位的女性数量与男性一样多。

options.sourceText: There is a remarkable difference across continents.
options.reflowSourceText: There is a remarkable difference across continents.
options.translationZh: 各大洲之间存在显着差异。

options.sourceText: There has been a marked increase in most countries.
options.reflowSourceText: There has been a marked increase in most countries.
options.translationZh: 大多数国家都有显着增长。

options.sourceText: The increase in people’s height has been quickening.
options.reflowSourceText: The increase in people’s height has been quickening.
options.translationZh: 人们的身高增长速度不断加快。

options.sourceText: The increase in women’s height is bigger than in men’s.
options.reflowSourceText: The increase in women’s height is bigger than in men’s.
options.translationZh: 女性身高增长幅度大于男性。

options.sourceText: It counts less than generally thought.
options.reflowSourceText: It counts less than generally thought.
options.translationZh: 它的重要性低于普遍认为的。

options.sourceText: It outweighs nutrition and healthcare.
options.reflowSourceText: It outweighs nutrition and healthcare.
options.translationZh: 它比营养和保健更重要。

options.sourceText: It impacts more on an individual than on population.
options.reflowSourceText: It impacts more on an individual than on population.
options.translationZh: 它对个人的影响大于对人口的影响。

options.sourceText: It plays a more significant role in females than in males.
options.reflowSourceText: It plays a more significant role in females than in males.
options.translationZh: 它在女性中比在男性中发挥更重要的作用。

options.sourceText: They tend to live longer.
options.reflowSourceText: They tend to live longer.

options.sourceText: They enjoy an easier life.
options.reflowSourceText: They enjoy an easier life.
options.translationZh: 他们享受更轻松的生活。

options.sourceText: They generally risk fewer fatal diseases.
options.reflowSourceText: They generally risk fewer fatal diseases.
options.translationZh: 他们通常患致命疾病的风险较少。

options.sourceText: They have greater expectations in life.
options.reflowSourceText: They have greater expectations in life.
options.translationZh: 他们对生活有更大的期望。

options.sourceText: They grow up slower than their peers in other countries.
options.reflowSourceText: They grow up slower than their peers in other countries.
options.translationZh: 他们比其他国家的同龄人成长得慢。

options.sourceText: They are actually shorter than their earlier generations.
options.reflowSourceText: They are actually shorter than their earlier generations.
options.translationZh: 他们实际上比前几代人要矮。

options.sourceText: They find it hard to bring their potential into full play.
options.reflowSourceText: They find it hard to bring their potential into full play.
options.translationZh: 他们发现自己的潜力很难得到充分发挥。

options.sourceText: They have experienced many changes of government
options.reflowSourceText: They have experienced many changes of government
options.translationZh: 他们经历了多次政府更迭

options.sourceText: Watch closely the global trend in children’s development.
options.reflowSourceText: Watch closely the global trend in children’s development.
options.translationZh: 密切关注全球儿童发展趋势。

options.sourceText: Make sure that our children grow up to their full height.
options.reflowSourceText: Make sure that our children grow up to their full height.
options.translationZh: 确保我们的孩子长到最大的高度。

options.sourceText: Try every means possible to improve our environment.
options.reflowSourceText: Try every means possible to improve our environment.
options.translationZh: 尽一切可能改善我们的环境。

options.sourceText: Ensure our children grow up in an ideal environment.
options.reflowSourceText: Ensure our children grow up in an ideal environment.
options.translationZh: 确保我们的孩子在理想的环境中成长。
